headline: Bangladesh observes Eid-e-Miladunnabi to mark birth and death of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
summary: The country observes the holy day with religious solemnity, national programs, and special prayers at mosques across the nation.
details: Bangladesh is observing the holy Eid-e-Miladunnabi today, commemorating both the birth and death anniversary of Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (PBUH).
Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was born in Makkah on the 12th of Rabiul Awal in 570 AD, bringing a message of peace for mankind, and passed away on the same date in 632 AD.
The government has organized extensive national-level programs to mark the public holiday, including hoisting the national flag at all government, semi-government, and autonomous institutions.
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman issued separate messages greeting Muslims worldwide on the occasion.
The president also inaugurated the Islamic Foundation’s fortnight-long “Siratunnabi (PBUH) Programme” at the Baitul Mukarram National Mosque in Dhaka.
Special prayers are being offered at mosques nationwide, including the Bangladesh Secretariat Mosque, while Bangladesh missions abroad are also observing the day.

topic: UN concern over minorities in India
headline_marked: UN watchdog [[rebukes India over discrimination]] against minorities
headline: UN watchdog rebukes India over discrimination against minorities
summary: The Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) warns of extrajudicial killings and hate crimes against Bengali-speaking Muslims and Dalits.
details: The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) has issued a stern warning to India, urging the country to better protect tribal peoples and disadvantaged castes.

The watchdog expressed grave concern over reports of large-scale violations by law enforcement officials against ethnic and ethno-religious groups, including Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes, particularly Dalits.
The committee specifically highlighted the urgent need for India to address hate crimes targeting Bengali-speaking Muslims.
Reported violations include racially motivated violence, excessive use of force, extrajudicial killings, arbitrary and prolonged detention without due process, and torture.
The UN body also noted reports of ill-treatment and sexual violence perpetrated by law enforcement officials against these marginalized groups.
CERD has called on the Indian government to investigate all allegations of abuse and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.
The report emphasizes that caste continues to be a primary determinant of social status in India, severely limiting access to education and opportunity for many.
caption:
The UN has issued a stern rebuke to India over reports of extrajudicial killings and hate crimes against minorities.

The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (CERD) has issued a stern warning to India, urging the country to better protect tribal peoples and disadvantaged castes.

The watchdog expressed grave concern over reports of large-scale violations by law enforcement officials against ethnic and ethno-religious groups, including Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes, particularly Dalits.

The committee specifically highlighted the urgent need for India to address hate crimes targeting Bengali-speaking Muslims.

Reported violations include racially motivated violence, excessive use of force, extrajudicial killings, arbitrary and prolonged detention without due process, and torture.

The UN body also noted reports of ill-treatment and sexual violence perpetrated by law enforcement officials against these marginalized groups.

CERD has called on the Indian government to investigate all allegations of abuse and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice.

The report emphasizes that caste continues to be a primary determinant of social status in India, severely limiting access to education and opportunity for many.
